{"type":"block-end","index":2,"block":{"type":"tool-call","id":"call_00_WzmdMNOkjl4AeQj81BGI9187","name":"write","arguments":"{\"file_path\": \"docs/intro.md\", \"content\": \"# Stream Agent Introduction\\n\\nThe stream agent is a lightweight runtime that consumes a single ordered stream of\\nevents and turns them into agent actions. It reads the stream incrementally, so it\\ncan react to new input as soon as it arrives rather than waiting for a complete\\npayload. This makes it suitable for interactive sessions where latency matters.\\n\\nThe agent keeps a small amount of state between events and exposes that state to\\nthe tool layer. Tools such as file writers and readers are invoked from within the\\nstream, which means the agent can inspect and modify the workspace in the middle of\\na conversation without any out-of-band coordination. All I/O is funneled through a\\nsingle protocol so behaviour stays predictable and auditable.\\n\\nBecause the design avoids branching streams, it is straightforward to reason about\\nordering and failure recovery. If an event is malformed the agent surfaces a clear\\nerror and continues with the next event, and any partial work is reported to the\\ncaller. The result is a small, dependable building block that can be embedded in\\nlarger harnesses without hidden coupling.\\n\"}"}}

{"type":"block-end","index":3,"block":{"type":"tool-call","id":"call_01_Y1zeZ2xoU10aHaSO2Obm8300","name":"write","arguments":"{\"file_path\": \"docs/design.md\", \"content\": \"# Single-Stream Protocol Design Notes\\n\\nThe protocol uses one ordered stream in each direction, carrying typed frames for\\nprompts, tool calls, tool results, and final answers. Ordering is guaranteed by the\\ntransport, so the protocol itself does not need sequence numbers for correctness;\\ntimestamps are recorded only for diagnostics.\\n\\nTwo tools are central to the design:\\n\\n- `tf-write` appends a payload to the workspace under the current run directory.\\n  The write is atomic per frame, and the tool returns the resolved path so the\\n  caller can verify what was created.\\n- `tf-peek` returns a bounded window of an existing file without mutating it. It\\n  is used to confirm that a previous `tf-write` landed and to inspect context\\n  before a follow-up edit.\\n\\nTool calls are synchronous from the agent's point of view: the stream pauses until\\n`tf-write` or `tf-peek` returns exactly one result frame. Errors are represented as\\nresult frames with a non-zero status rather than as stream resets, which keeps the\\nprotocol simple and lets the agent recover without reconnecting. Backpressure is\\nhandled by the transport; the protocol never buffers an unbounded number of\\nframes, and a slow consumer simply slows the producer.\\n\"}"}}

{"type":"block-end","index":4,"block":{"type":"tool-call","id":"call_02_iClcEGMTEp7V4FeOxbid1822","name":"write","arguments":"{\"file_path\": \"docs/eval.md\", \"content\": \"# Evaluation Plan Summary\\n\\nThe evaluation plan defines a compact set of metrics, tracked under METRICS, that\\nmeasure both task success and protocol efficiency. Each run records outcomes for\\nevery scenario so that results can be compared across configurations without\\nre-deriving numbers by hand.\\n\\nPrimary METRICS include task completion rate, number of tool calls per task, total\\ntokens consumed, wall-clock latency, and recovery rate after malformed input. The\\nbaseline is the current single-stream implementation with default settings; every\\nchange is compared against that baseline using the same scenarios and machine.\\n\\nRuns are deterministic where possible: fixtures are fixed, and any randomness is\\nseeded and recorded alongside the results. A change is considered an improvement\\nonly if it improves completion rate or latency without regressing token usage\\nbeyond the agreed tolerance. Results are archived per run so the baseline can be\\nrecomputed whenever the harness is updated.\\n\"}"}}

{"type":"block-end","index":5,"block":{"type":"tool-call","id":"call_03_JvsXwa32SPzDiG6Fhr2k0081","name":"write","arguments":"{\"file_path\": \"docs/roadmap.md\", \"content\": \"# Roadmap\\n\\n- M0: Freeze the scope and record the baseline behaviour of the current harness.\\n- M1: Specify the single-stream frame format and document all frame types.\\n- M2: Implement the core stream reader and the ordered event loop.\\n- M3: Add the `tf-write` tool with atomic per-frame writes.\\n- M4: Add the `tf-peek` tool with bounded windows and no mutation.\\n- M5: Wire tool calls into the stream with one result frame per call.\\n- M6: Add error result frames and recovery on malformed input.\\n- M7: Build the fixture-driven evaluation scenarios and METRICS reporting.\\n- M8: Run the first full comparison against the recorded baseline.\\n- M9: Harden backpressure handling and add streaming diagnostics.\\n- M10: Publish the design notes, evaluation summary, and a stable release.\\n\"}"}}
